key_gap: Both sides produced the same closing attribution (promos −2.2 / mix −1.6 / freight −1.1 / COGS −0.8 / returns −0.7 / fees −0.6 = −7.0), the same ranking (impact × controllability × testability), and the same falsifiable first test (8-week matched-product promo hold-out), but the human opened with the margin identity and built the MECE tree first-pass with mix as a first-class branch, while the AI derived the tree across two passes and self-corrected a promo×mix double-count (initially −2.6/−1.2) only because the sum-to-−7.0 check caught it. On a data-complete attribution problem, the identity IS the frame, and the AI's staged reconstruction was overhead.
learning_signal: When the task is attribution of a change in a KPI, the defining identity (Margin = Revenue − COGS − Freight − Returns − Fees; Revenue = Price × Volume × Mix) IS the MECE frame — build the tree first-pass from it, make mix its own branch (the classic miss), quantify every branch from the data, and require the attribution to close against the observed change; then prioritize by expected impact × controllability × testability (not size alone), state the #1 hypothesis falsifiably with a test design and success metric, and hold untested branches. The close-the-arithmetic check (sum = observed change, no double-count) is the completeness gate — promo depth must be attributed with mix held constant.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'tree-first, close-the-arithmetic' discipline to WHAT/WHY for decomposition tasks: (a) emit the defining identity as the frame before any analysis; (b) enumerate branches MECE from it (mix as its own branch); (c) attribute each branch from supplied data with a no-double-count rule (measure each driver holding the others constant); (d) require sum-of-branches = observed change within tolerance before leaving WHY — an open residual triggers the NEG-01 path (missing-branch hunt) instead of being logged as noise; (e) prioritize by impact × controllability × testability; (f) end with one falsifiable hypothesis + test design + quantified expected recovery.

key_gap: The pure style built the tree from the supplied branches, force-fit the 18pt unexplained residual to the Q3 rebates restatement ('measurement noise'), pruned the renegotiated top-account program as immaterial-to-averages (8% of category revenue), and recommended freight/COGS cost-cutting — attacking the ~1pt explained branch while the verified root cause sat in the packet. The AI treated the residual as a completeness alarm (the tree is not collectively exhaustive), falsified the restatement decoy (a timing item nets to ~0 by construction), traced the missing 'terms' branch to the verified contract memo, and recommended terms governance with quantified recovery. The pure style's documented weaknesses — tree too rigid, premature pruning — operated exactly as registered.
learning_signal: The tree is a hypothesis about the structure of the problem, not the problem itself: when branch attribution does not sum to the observed change, the tree is incomplete, not the data noisy. Before pruning any branch or prioritizing the largest explained one, run a residual reconciliation: if |observed − Σbranches| > ~10–15% of the change, force a missing-branch hunt and disaggregate below the averages (account/product-level sub-tree — averages mask bimodal distributions); verify any 'one-time/noise' explanation against its construction (an accounting timing item cannot be a 12-month margin leak); prune only after the residual is reconciled to a verified cause. Impact measured on category averages is a prior, not a ceiling on concentrated anomalies.
suggested_improvement: Add a mandatory 'residual reconciliation' step to WHY (and REVIEW for any attribution-like task): (a) after attribution, compute the open residual explicitly; (b) residual > ~10% of the observed change → enter a missing-branch hunt before any prioritization/pruning — enumerate what the current tree cannot express (terms, programs, account-level concentration, one-off events); (c) verify 'noise' explanations by construction (timing items, restatements, sampling) rather than accepting them; (d) disaggregate to account/product level when category averages are stable but the metric moves; (e) only then prioritize and prune, and log the residual's verified disposition.
